source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3--4, Assumptions 1--2; p. 7, Theorem 4; p. 8, Theorem 5; pp. 9--10, discussion of Theorem 6
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper assumes a score density continuous and bounded away from zero, proves uniform distance-estimator convergence and uniform Gaussian-band coverage, and gives a lower bound for scalar-distance isotropic estimators.

source_verification_receipts.version: journal-version reproduction, Mathematical Methods of Statistics 14 (2005); arXiv v3
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1--3, Theorems 1--2 and severe Gamma-varying example
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies pointwise random-design regression with vanishing density; its Gamma-varying example with exp(-1/h^alpha) has logarithmically slow minimax convergence.
The paper uses a local-polynomial estimator with a Lepski-type data-driven bandwidth selector for pointwise adaptation to unknown local design scarcity and smoothness.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv preprint corresponding to Statistics & Probability Letters 77 (2007), 782--794
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper constructs an unknown-design-density estimator with a spatially dependent sup-norm normalization and proposes an inhomogeneous confidence band under positive continuous design density.

The paper studies random-design uniform loss with design-density vanishing points, constructs a design- and smoothness-adaptive estimator, and develops an optimality criterion for spatially deformed rates.
The paper considers known univariate design densities with a finite number of well-separated polynomial or exponential zeros and global L2 minimax lower bounds plus adaptive wavelet estimators.
The paper develops Gaussian anti-concentration and multiplier-bootstrap honest bands, including data-driven resolution selection.
The paper develops bias-aware honest scalar intervals for nonparametric regression and derives efficiency bounds and optimal bandwidths.
The paper gives pointwise k-NN adaptation using local ball-mass growth and locally selected neighborhood size.
